To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the risk of major haemsorrhage in patients treated with oral anticoaquants after infrainguinial venous bypass surgery can be predicted by age, diabetes and hypertension and that this risk can be reduced by treatment with aspirin.

patients with an increased systolic bloodpressure, an age of 75 years or more and diabetes mellitus have a higher risk of major haemmorrhage after venous bypass surgery and that this risk can be reduced by using aspirin instead of anticoagulation.
the risk of major haemsorrhage in patients on oral antithrombotics after infrainguinal bypass can be predicted by the presence of hypertension, advanced age, and diabetes mellitus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the risk of bleeding complications in patients with peripheral arterial occlusive disease (PAD) treated by bypass surgery.
the development and evaluation of methods for the treatment of patients with chronic venous disease and venous ulcers, and with the development and testing of a new type of artificial blood vessel.

the prevention of thrombotic complications of peripheral vascular disease, in particular the prevention of graft occlusion after peripheral vascular surgery and the prevention of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism in patients with peripheral vascular disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Dutch Bypass Anticoagulation Or Aspirin study has not provided sufficient information to make any recommendation for or against the use of aspirin after peripheral arterial bypass surgery.
the use of anticoagulatants is not justified in the treatment of patients with infra-inguinal venous by-pass surgery.
the risk benefit ratio of oral anticoaculation after infrainguinal bypass is still favourable, but that patients at highest risk for major hemorrhage should be considered for alternative treatment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a model that identifies patients at risk of major bleeding complications after infrainguinal bypass grafting.
we recommend treatment with oral anti-coagulants after venous bypass surgery, but we advise to treat patients with high systolic blood pressure with aspirin.
aspirin is a safe antithrombotic drug after venous bypass surgery, but that oral anticoagulant treatment should be preferred.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we should not use the risk of major bleeding to decide between aspirin and anticoagulation.
the use of aspirin after peripheral venous surgery is not recommended.
patients with a venous bypass are at higher risk of haemorrhage if they receive oral anticoagulation.
